source_spans.exact_narration: Here on New Call, an authorized dispatcher is preparing a fictional community standby. The Name identifies it as training, and Nature explains the exercise. Priority is Routine and Type is Medical. Use a clear description and the choices that fit your department. These details help the next dispatcher understand the scheduled work without treating this example as a real incident.

source_spans.exact_narration: In Select Dispatch Recipients, Wallace Boden is the one checked person. Everyone is unchecked, and the footer confirms one selected. Check both the name and the count before choosing Confirm. This training account has No location, so this selection does not demonstrate a nearest-person calculation. The point here is to keep the planned dispatch list specific.

source_spans.exact_narration: Call updated successfully appears on the same training call. The Scheduled for banner and Info row now show eleven thirty in the morning in the department clock. That is the saved result of choosing nine thirty on this device. The call is still scheduled. Use this pattern for a fire or EMS standby, a community paramedicine or mental-health coordination exercise, a search-and-rescue briefing, planned security support, a wildland contractor drill, or industrial response-team training. Agree on the event time, select the intended recipients, save the schedule, and read back the department time on the call.
